   363	private theorem tendsto_zero_of_forall_approx {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {F : ι → ℝ}
   364	    (h : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ G : ι → ℝ, Filter.Tendsto G l (nhds 0) ∧ ∀ i, |F i - G i| ≤ ε) :

     1	\section{Occupation bounds for the intrinsic constant}
     2	\label{S:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling}
     3	
     4	Retain all original models and amplitudes, put $a = \alpha_0$, $q = 4-\alpha >
     5	2$, $k = 3-\alpha = q-1 > 1$ and $m = q/k$. The temporal kernel is $K(s,t) =
     6	|s-t|^{-a}$ on $I = (0,1)$; its diagonal value may be set to zero. Let
     7	$\mathcal{O}$ be the full strongly $H^1$-measurable unit-profile class defined
     8	before Proposition~\ref{P:occupation-physical-class}. Here we use the
     9	\emph{original} kernel, defining
    10	\begin{equation}\label{E:raw-occupation-definitions}
    11	  \begin{aligned}
    12	    A(g)&=\int_{I^2}K(s,t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,\\
    13	    C_{\rm occ}&=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}
    14	    \frac{A(g)}{T(g)^{\alpha/2}},&
    15	    \mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}
    16	    &=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\{A(g)-\zeta T(g)\},\qquad \zeta>0.
    17	  \end{aligned}
    18	\end{equation}
    19	The scalar penalty $\zeta$ is not a spatial mask. These objects differ from the
    20	earlier damped-kernel energy. Assume $\Gamma \ne 0$ until the direct zero case
    21	below.
    22	
    23	\begin{lemma}[Full-profile squares in the original space]
    24	  \label{L:occupation-raw-square}
    25	  There is a continuous map $Q:H^1(\R^d;\R) \to H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ with
    26	  \[
    27	    \langle Q(f),Q(h)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    28	    =B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2),\qquad
    29	    \|Q(f)\|^2=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f).
    30	  \]
    31	  For $g \in \mathcal{O}$, the element $\rho_g = J_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}(s\mapsto
    32	  Q(g_s))$ belongs to the original $H_I$ and satisfies
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-raw-identities}
    34	    \|\rho_g\|_{H_I}^2=A(g),\qquad
    35	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}
    36	    =\int_I\int_{\R^d}h_{\Psi,s}(x)g_s(x)^2\ud x\ud s
    37	  \end{equation}
    38	  for every $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$. In particular,
    39	  \[
    40	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}\le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g)}.
    41	  \]
    42	\end{lemma}
    43	
    44	\begin{proof}
    45	  Approximate $f$ in $H^1$ by real compact smooth $f_n$.
    46	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} gives
    47	  \[
    48	    \|f_n^2-f_l^2\|_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}^2
    49	    =C_4(f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l,f_n-f_l,f_n+f_l)
    50	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}N(f_n-f_l)^2N(f_n+f_l)^2\to0.
    51	  \]
    52	  Here $N$ is continuous on $H^1$ and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. Completeness
    53	  defines $Q(f)$; interlacing two approximating sequences proves independence.
    54	  Passing the physical four-linear continuity and Hilbert pairings to limits
    55	  proves the first identities. The same difference bound, first for smooth
    56	  approximants and then by passage to the limit, proves continuity of $Q$.
    57	
    58	  Thus, $F_g(s) = Q(g_s)$ is strongly measurable. Writing $b_s = \|\nabla
    59	  g_s\|_2^2$, the unit norm and $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$ give
    60	  \[
    61	    \int_I\|F_g(s)\|^2\ud s
    62	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}\int_I b_s^{\alpha/2}\ud s
    63	    \le R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty .
    64	  \]
    65	  Lemma~\ref{L:positive-raw-embedding} now constructs $\rho_g$ and identifies
    66	  its squared norm with the physical $A(g)$. Joint measurability and
    67	  representative independence follow from the continuous physical pairing on
    68	  $(H^1)^2$. Absolute time integrability follows from the same Schur bound.
    69	
    70	  Choose one compact smooth $\chi$ equal to one on all spatial supports of
    71	  $\Psi_t$. For real $f \in H^1$, smooth approximation gives
    72	  \[
    73	    \langle\Psi_t,Q(f)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    74	    =\lim_n B_\Gamma(\Psi_t,f_n^2)
    75	    =C_4(\chi,\Psi_t,f,f)=B_\Gamma(\Psi_t,f^2).
    76	  \]
    77	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} justifies these absolute integrals and
    78	  limits. Polarizing~\eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion} gives
    79	  \[
    80	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle
    81	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle\Psi_t,Q(g_s)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    82	    \ud t\ud s .
    83	  \]
    84	  The absolute integrand is bounded by the product of two $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$
    85	  norms against $K$, integrable by Schur and $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz. Evenness of
    86	  $\Gamma$ and Tonelli for the nonnegative physical integrands
    87	  yield~\eqref{E:occupation-raw-identities}. Hilbert Cauchy--Schwarz with
    88	  $\|\Psi\|^2 = v_\Psi$ proves the bound. No rough occupation is inserted into a
    89	  stochastic flow. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-raw-square}.
    90	\end{proof}

    92	\begin{proposition}[Original occupation energy and dilation]
    93	  \label{P:raw-occupation-energy}
    94	  With $K_0 = 2^a/(1-a)$,
    95	  \[
    96	    0<C_{\rm occ}\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty .
    97	  \]
    98	  Moreover,
    99	  \begin{align}
   100	    \mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}
   101	    &=D_\zeta C_{\rm occ}^{2/(2-\alpha)},&
   102	    D_\zeta&=\frac{2-\alpha}{2}
   103	    \left(\frac{\alpha}{2\zeta}\right)^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)},
   104	    \label{E:raw-occupation-energy}\\
   105	    C_{\rm occ}
   106	    &=\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}}{2-\alpha}\right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}
   107	    \left(\frac{2\zeta}{\alpha}\right)^{\alpha/2}.
   108	    \label{E:raw-occupation-ratio}
   109	  \end{align}
   110	  In particular, $\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}} > 0$ is finite and equals
   111	  $\zeta^{-\alpha/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_1^{\mathcal{O}}$.
   112	\end{proposition}
   113	
   114	\begin{proof}
   115	  A unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy: a zero weak gradient makes
   116	  it constant, and an $L^2$ constant on $\R^d$ is zero. Hence, $0 < T(g) <
   117	  \infty$. Spatial covariance Cauchy--Schwarz gives $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   118	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}b_s^{\alpha/4}b_t^{\alpha/4}$. Schur with row bound $K_0$, then
   119	  concavity, proves
   120	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-occupation-bound}
   121	    0\le A(g)\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}.
   122	  \end{equation}
   123	  A fixed compact smooth unit profile, constant in time, belongs to
   124	  $\mathcal{O}$ and has positive $A$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   125	  This proves positivity and finiteness of $C_{\rm occ}$.
   126	
   127	  The map $(U_\ell g)_s(x) = \ell^{d/2}g_s(\ell x)$ is an $H^1$ isomorphism
   128	  preserving unit mass and strong measurability. It has inverse $U_{1/\ell}$ and
   129	  is a bijection on $\mathcal{O}$. The physical Radon change of variables gives
   130	  \[
   131	    A(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A(g),\qquad
   132	    T(U_\ell g)=\ell^2T(g).
   133	  \]

   135	  $\ell^{-d}$, and the pushforward of $\Gamma$ contributes $\ell^{\alpha-d}$.

   137	  $g,\ell$ leaves the class unchanged. For fixed $A,T > 0$, the derivative of

   140	  T))^{1/(2-\alpha)}$ and equals $D_\zeta[A/T^{\alpha/2}]^{2/(2-\alpha)}$. For
   141	  $A = 0$ the supremum is zero as $\ell\downarrow0$. Bounding every ratio by
   142	  $C_{\rm occ}$ gives one inequality in~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-energy}. Fixed
   143	  ratios approaching its positive supremum give the other by continuity of the
   144	  positive power. Algebra gives~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-ratio} and the penalty
   145	  scaling. No optimizer or minimax interchange is assumed. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-occupation-energy}.
   147	\end{proof}

   149	\begin{lemma}[Countable Rayleigh near-occupations]
   150	  \label{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection}
   151	  For fixed $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$
   152	  there is $g_\varepsilon \in \mathcal{O}$ such that
   153	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-rayleigh-selection}
   154	    I_\Psi^2+T(g_\varepsilon)
   155	    \le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g_\varepsilon)}+\varepsilon .
   156	  \end{equation}
   157	\end{lemma}
   158	
   159	\begin{proof}
   160	  The real $H^1$ space is separable, for example by its isometric embedding
   161	  $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ into a finite product of $L^2$ spaces. Compact smooth

    23	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian envelope for the original covariance]
    24	  \label{L:variational-heat-envelope}

    26	  (2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2\epsilon)}$,
    27	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-heat-envelope}
    28	    (\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    29	    =\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}\mu(\ud\xi),
    30	    \qquad
    31	    0\le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    32	    \le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(0)<\infty.
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  The value at zero is strictly positive.

    37	\begin{proof}
    38	  A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial ball growth. Indeed, evaluate
    39	  its tempered bound on a nonnegative smooth cutoff equal to one on $B_1$,
    40	  dilated by $R \ge 1$. Its finitely many Schwartz seminorms are bounded by
    41	  $CR^N$, so positivity gives a ball-mass bound $CR^N$. Summing dyadic annuli
    42	  shows that $(1+|x|)^{-L}$ is integrable for $L > N$. Apply this separately to
    43	  $\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Gaussian weights are therefore integrable against both
    44	  measures. The classical convolution on the left is finite and smooth locally
    45	  in $x$: on compact $x$ sets its translated Gaussian derivatives are bounded by
    46	  any fixed sufficiently fast polynomial weight in the integration variable.
    47	
    48	  Pair the convolution with a Schwartz test $\varphi$. Absolute Fubini is
    49	  justified by these weights. The resulting pairing is that of $\Gamma$ with
    50	  $p_\epsilon*\varphi$. Applying the spectral convention in
    51	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} and the identity $\int p_\epsilon(y)e^{-i\xi\cdot
    52	  y}\ud y = e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}$ gives exactly the right side
    53	  of~\eqref{E:variational-heat-envelope} as a distribution. The heat kernel is
    54	  even, so either Fourier sign gives that same Gaussian multiplier. Its spectral
    55	  integral is absolutely finite and continuous in $x$ by dominated convergence.
    56	  Thus, equality of the two continuous distributions gives equality at every
    57	  $x$, without an extra normalization factor. The physical convolution is
    58	  nonnegative. Evenness of $\mu$ makes the spectral integral real, and its
    59	  absolute value is bounded by its total Gaussian mass, the value at zero.
    60	  Finally, $\Gamma \ne 0$ and $p_\epsilon > 0$ give strict positivity there.
    61	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope}.
    62	\end{proof}

   805	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
   806	  in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
   807	  $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
   808	  \[
   809	    N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
   810	    N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
   811	    N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
   812	    \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
   813	  \]
   814	  Let
   815	  \[
   816	    K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   817	    \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   818	  \]
   819	  Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
   820	  $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   821	  $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   822	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   823	    N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   824	    N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   825	  \end{equation}
   826	  More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
   827	  $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
   828	  by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
   829	  $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
   830	  and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
   831	  \[
   832	    K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   833	    \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   834	  \]
   835	  Then, for every $\theta>0$,
   836	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
   837	    \begin{split}
   838	      0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
   839	      0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
   840	    \end{split}
   841	  \end{equation}
   842	  These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
   843	  domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
   844	  scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
   845	  Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
   846	  give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is
   847	  unchanged by Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel.
   848	\end{lemma}

   850	\begin{proof}
   851	  Scaling the Fourier representation of $\Gamma$ and using Fourier uniqueness
   852	  gives $\mu(cA) = c^\alpha\mu(A)$. Radon finiteness and $\alpha > 0$ then imply
   853	  $\mu(\{0\}) = 0$. In particular, $\mu(B_r) = r^\alpha V$, where $V = \mu(B_1)
   854	  < \infty$. Therefore, for $a > 0$,
   855	  \[
   856	    \int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{a^2+|\xi|^2}
   857	    =\alpha V a^{\alpha-2}
   858	    \int_0^\infty\frac{u^{\alpha-1}}{1+u^2}\ud u<\infty.
   859	  \]
   860	  The last integral is finite since $0 < \alpha < 2$. Substitution into $N_1$
   861	  reduces its finiteness to
   862	  $\int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}(\theta+\lambda)^{\alpha-2} \ud\lambda <
   863	  \infty$: the conditions at zero and infinity are $\alpha_0 > 0$ and
   864	  $\alpha+\alpha_0 < 2$.
   865	
   866	  For $N_2$ use $|\widehat{G}_s(\xi)| \le \min(s,|\xi|^{-1})$. On $|\xi| \le 1$,
   867	  absolute integration is bounded by
   868	  \[
   869	    V\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   870	    e^{-\theta(s+t)}|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}st\ud s\ud t<\infty.
   871	  \]
   872	  On $|\xi| > 1$, use $\int_{|\xi|>1}|\xi|^{-2}\mu(\ud\xi) = \alpha
   873	  V/(2-\alpha)$ and the same time integral without $st$. Both time integrals are
   874	  finite by splitting into $s \le t$ and $t \le s$, then using $u = \min(s,t)$
   875	  and $v = |s-t|$; the only singular factor is $v^{-\alpha_0}$, with $\alpha_0 <
   876	  1$. This proves absolute integrability of the displayed spectral formula. For
   877	  each $\xi$, its time integral is nonnegative because the temporal kernel is
   878	  positive definite. Indeed, it is a positive Laplace mixture of the kernels
   879	  $e^{-\lambda|s-t|}$. This proves $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$.
   880	
   881	  The mass identity $G_s(\R^d) = s$ proves the formula for $N_0$. In $N_1$
   882	  change $\lambda = \theta u$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$. In $N_2$ change $s =
   883	  u/\theta$, $t = v/\theta$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$, using
   884	  $\widehat{G}_{u/\theta}(\theta\eta) = \theta^{-1}\widehat{G}_u(\eta)$. These
   885	  changes give exactly the stated powers.

   887	  The first tail in~\eqref{E:damped-tail-norms} is a tail of the finite
   888	  nonnegative $N_1(1)$ integral. For the second, $0 \le K_M(r) \le
   889	  |r|^{-\alpha_0}$ and $K_M(r) \to 0$ for $r \ne 0$. The absolute majorant just
   890	  proved permits dominated convergence in $(s,t,\xi)$, giving $N_2^{(M)}(1)^2
   891	  \to 0$. The tail kernel is positive definite by the same Laplace-mixture
   892	  argument, so its quadratic form is nonnegative.
   893	
   894	  For the multiplier comparisons, define
   895	  \[
   896	    B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   897	    e^{-\theta(s+t)}e^{-\lambda|s-t|}
   898	    \widehat G_s(\xi)\overline{\widehat G_t(\xi)}\ud s\ud t.
   899	  \]

   901	  $e^{-\lambda|s-t|}$ gives $B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)\ge0$.
   902	  The absolute-integrability bound above, $0\le m\le1$ and
   903	  $0\le K_S\le|\cdot|^{-\alpha_0}$ justify changing the integration order:
   904	  \[
   905	    N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2
   906	    =\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   907	    \int_S\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}
   908	    \int m(\xi)B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)\mu(\ud\xi)\ud\lambda.
   909	  \]

   911	  in~\eqref{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}. It is used after time integration,
   912	  not pointwise on the oscillating product of wave Fourier kernels. The first
   913	  comparison follows directly from the nonnegative integrand defining $N_1$.
   914	  The choices $S=(0,\infty)$ or $S=(M,\infty)$ give the full or tail bounds.
   915	  Gaussian spatial and Green smoothing contribute products of multipliers in
   916	  $[0,1]$ depending only on $\xi$. Gaussian Green smoothing also preserves
   917	  $G_s(\R^d)=s$, proving its separate assertion for $N_0$. This proves
   918	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}.
   919	\end{proof}

   921	\paragraph{Covariance pairings of translated kernels.}
   922	Fix $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. Let $\mu$ be a finite positive Borel measure on $\R^d$
   923	such that $\gamma(z) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}\mu(\ud\xi)$ is real and nonnegative
   924	for every $z$. Thus, $\gamma$ is bounded, continuous and even, with $0 \le
   925	\gamma(z) \le \mu(\R^d)$. Let $\nu$ be a positive Borel measure on $(0,\infty)$
   926	with $\nu((0,L]) < \infty$ for every $L > 0$, and put
   927	\[
   928	  \kappa_L(t)=\int_{(0,L]}e^{-\lambda|t|}\nu(\ud\lambda),\qquad
   929	  C_L((t,x),(s,y))=\kappa_L(t-s)\gamma(x-y).
   930	\]

   522	structure FreeWaveData (d : ℕ) (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] where
   523	  /-- The free group `S_E(t)`. -/

   525	  S_zero : S 0 = 1
   526	  S_add : ∀ s t, S (s + t) = S s * S t
   527	  /-- The velocity reversal. -/
   528	  R : E →L[ℝ] E
   529	  R_norm : ∀ z, ‖R z‖ = ‖z‖

   531	  /-- The translations `τ_y`. -/
   532	  τ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → E →L[ℝ] E
   533	  τ_norm : ∀ y z, ‖τ y z‖ = ‖z‖
   534	  τ_comm : ∀ y h, S h * τ y = τ y * S h

   539	`U(t,s) - I` along some nontrivial filter of partitions.  A partition is a pair
   540	`(n, p)` with points `p 0, …, p n`; only the points `p j`, `j ≤ n`, enter, and they lie
   541	in `[s,t]` eventually.  The TeX's convergence as the mesh tends to zero implies this

   546	    (∀ᶠ π in l, ∀ j ≤ π.1, π.2 j ∈ Set.Icc s t) ∧
   547	    Tendsto (fun π => youngSum X U s π.2 π.1) l (𝓝 (U t s - 1))

  3600	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}
  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]
  3610	  These Bochner integrals exist in $L^2(\Omega)$ and satisfy
  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}
  3616	  For $m+n = 2k$, concatenate $\boldsymbol\tau =
  3617	  (s_1,\ldots,s_m,r_1,\ldots,r_n)$ and $\boldsymbol\eta =
  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then
  3619	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-wick-formula}
  3620	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),
  3622	  \end{equation}
  3623	  where, with both chains terminating at $(T,x)$,
  3624	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-pairing-integral}
  3625	    \begin{split}
  3626	      \mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}
  3627	      ={}&\int_{[0,T]^m_<\times[0,T]^n_<}
  3628	      \ud\boldsymbol s\,\ud\boldsymbol r
  3629	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\
  3630	      &\quad\times\prod_{j=1}^m
  3631	      G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j)
  3632	      \prod_{j=1}^n
  3633	      G_{r_{j+1}-r_j}(z_{j+1}-\ud z_j)\\
  3634	      &\quad\times\prod_{\{a,b\}\in D}
  3635	      \mathcal{K}(\tau_a,\eta_a;\tau_b,\eta_b).
  3636	    \end{split}
  3637	  \end{equation}
  3638	  Each pairing has coefficient one. If $m+n$ is odd, the expectation is zero.
  3639	  Empty chains and the case $m = n = 0$ have the usual empty-product meaning. If
  3640	  $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, every integral above is nonnegative. Consequently,
  3641	  entrywise comparison $0 \le \mathcal{K}_1 \le \mathcal{K}_2$ compares all
  3642	  finite partial-order second moments in the same direction. The series
  3643	  $\sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$ for every real or complex
  3644	  $r$.
  3645	\end{lemma}
  3646	
  3647	\begin{proof}
  3648	  The mass of $G_h$ is $h$. If $M_n(T)$ is the total mass of
  3649	  $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$, integration at the last vertex gives $M_0 = 1$ and
  3650	  $M_n(T) = \int_0^T(T-s)M_{n-1}(s)\ud s$. Induction therefore yields $M_n(T) =
  3651	  T^{2n}/(2n)!$. Gaussian moments and H\"older's inequality give
  3652	  \[
  3653	    \left\|\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\right\|_2
  3654	    \le\prod_{j=1}^n\|\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\|_{2n}
  3655	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}.
  3656	  \]
  3657	  Mean-square continuity of Gaussian variables implies their continuity in every
  3658	  fixed finite $L^p$. Hence, the product is strongly measurable in $L^2$ on the
  3659	  stated pieces. The finite kernel mass and the displayed bound prove Bochner
  3660	  integrability and~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}.
  3661	
  3662	  Fubini now passes expectation through the product of the two finite kernel
  3663	  measures. For the $m+n$ Gaussian variables at their labelled vertices,
  3664	  differentiate
  3665	  \[
  3666	    \E\exp\left(\sum_i t_i\mathcal{W}(\tau_i,\eta_i)\right)
  3667	    =\exp\left(\frac12\sum_{i,j}t_i t_j
  3668	    \mathcal{K}(\tau_i,\eta_i;\tau_j,\eta_j)\right)
  3669	  \]
  3670	  once in each $t_i$ at zero. Odd total degree gives zero. At degree $2k$ the
  3671	  result is the sum over unordered pair partitions, with one covariance product
  3672	  per pairing. Orientations and orderings of the $k$ pairs cancel the
  3673	  exponential's $2^k k!$ denominator. Integration
  3674	  gives~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula} with precisely the domains and
  3675	  coefficients in~\eqref{E:terminal-pairing-integral}.
  3676	
  3677	  Symmetrizing a chain measure does not change its stochastic integral: the
  3678	  product of its $n$ scalar field values is invariant under relabeling. Thus,
  3679	  averaging the $n!$ pushforwards of $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$ with coefficient
  3680	  $1/n!$ gives the same $Y_n$. There is no additional $n!$ factor
  3681	  in~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula}, or $m!n!$ in a two-chain product. This
  3682	  identifies the ordinary ordered regularized integrals and their symmetrized
  3683	  convention in~\eqref{E:expansion}.

  3686	  measures have the same masses and converge weakly to $G$. Off the finitely
  3687	  many time cut points, all finite Gaussian moments are bounded continuous
  3688	  functions of the spatial variables. Dominated convergence for their finite
  3689	  Wick sums proves the same limit for the mixed second moments with two Green
  3690	  widths. It gives $L^2$ convergence to the Bochner integral above, exactly the
  3691	  fixed-noise Green convention used in the source.
  3692	
  3693	  If $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, positivity of the Green measures makes each covariance
  3694	  product nonnegative. Comparing them proves the stated finite-moment
  3695	  monotonicity, including self-pairs and unequal chains. Finally, the ratio of
  3696	  successive right sides of~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}, with an additional
  3697	  factor $|r|^n$, is $|r|\sqrt V T^2/((2n+2)\sqrt{2n+1})$, which tends to zero.
  3698	  The zero-variance case is immediate. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick}.
  3699	\end{proof}

  3702	
  3703	\begin{lemma}[Uniform series tails from scaled moments]\label{L:uniform-series-tail}
  3704	  Fix $(T,x)$. For each positive regularization pair $(\epsilon,\delta)$, let
  3705	  $Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$ be the terms of Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} for a
  3706	  field with nonnegative covariance. Write $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r) =
  3707	  \sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$. Suppose that, for some $r > 1$ and
  3708	  finite $B_r$,
  3709	  \[
  3710	    \sup_{\epsilon,\delta>0}
  3711	    \E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r)|^2\le B_r,
  3712	    \qquad
  3713	    Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\longrightarrow X_n
  3714	    \text{ in }L^2\text{ for each fixed }n.
  3715	  \]
  3716	  Then $u = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$,
  3717	  $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1) \to u$ in $L^2$, and
  3718	  \begin{equation}\label{E:uniform-series-tail}
  3719	    \|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\|_2,\ \|X_n\|_2
  3720	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad
  3721	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\right\|_2,
  3722	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}X_n\right\|_2
  3723	    \le\frac{B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}.
  3724	  \end{equation}
  3725	  If also $\E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1)|^2 \le B_1$ uniformly, then $\E|u|^2 \le
  3726	  B_1$.
  3727	\end{lemma}
  3728	
  3729	\begin{proof}
  3730	  Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} gives absolute $L^2$ convergence of every
  3731	  regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. Its scaled second moment
  3732	  therefore contains the nonnegative term $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2$,
  3733	  so $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2 \le B_r$. Taking the fixed-order $L^2$
  3734	  limit proves the same bound for $X_n$. The geometric series and the triangle
  3735	  inequality give all estimates in~\eqref{E:uniform-series-tail}, including
  3736	  absolute convergence.
  3737	
  3738	  For each $N$, write both full series as their first $N+1$ terms and their
  3739	  tails. Their distance is at most
  3740	  \[
  3741	    \frac{2B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}
  3742	    +\left\|\sum_{n=0}^N(Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}-X_n)\right\|_2.
  3743	  \]
  3744	  First let $\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0$ at fixed $N$, and then let $N \to
  3745	  \infty$. This proves convergence of the full regularized solution; it was not
  3746	  assumed. Continuity of the $L^2$ norm passes the bound $B_1$ to $u$. This
  3747	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-series-tail}.
  3748	\end{proof}

     2	\label{S:actual-symplectic-phase}

     4	Retain the original model, covariance amplitude, physical mask $m_R$ and real $E
     5	= H^{1/2}\times H^{-1/2}$. Fix finite $R,T > 0$ and admissible exponents as
     6	in~\eqref{E:driver-parameters}. Let $M = M_R(W)$ be the from the given noise
     7	first interaction path on $E$, and $M^\rho$ its regularized paths from
     8	Proposition~\ref{P:source-gaussian-transfer} and the source construction. Here
     9	$\rho$ is the positive heat/Laplace smoothing pair. The construction preserving
    10	the given noise and ordinary rows are those of
    11	Lemma~\ref{L:source-retaining-isometry},
    12	Lemma~\ref{L:source-pointfield-regularity} and
    13	Proposition~\ref{P:source-ordinary-response}. The full $F$ operator path and
    14	Young evolution are fixed by Proposition~\ref{P:constant-phase-driver} and
    15	Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear}; their $E$ restrictions are used here.
    16	Complexifications commute with conjugation, so these real restrictions are the
    17	physical phases. For fixed $\Phi$ in the full positive-time original $H_W$ and
    18	real $c$ set
    19	\begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-combined-driver}
    20	  \begin{aligned}
    21	    Z&=W(\Phi),\qquad D_\Phi=\E[ZM],\qquad
    22	    D_\Phi^\rho=\E[ZM^\rho],\\
    23	    D&=cM+D_\Phi,\qquad D^\rho=cM^\rho+D_\Phi^\rho .
    24	  \end{aligned}
    25	\end{equation}
    26	All these are operator paths on $E$. The covariance mean is not a pointwise
    27	original potential. Write $U_D$ for left Young evolution and $P_D(t,s) =
    28	S_E(t)U_D(t,s)S_E(-s)$.
    29	
    30	\begin{lemma}[Free wave form and compact Young baseline]
    31	  \label{L:symplectic-free}
    32	  There is a bounded isometric skew-adjoint $J_E$ on $E$, with $J_E^2 = -I$,
    33	  such that
    34	  \[
    35	    \omega(z,w)=\langle z,J_Ew\rangle_E
    36	    =\langle u,g\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}}
    37	    -\langle f,v\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}},
    38	    \quad z=(u,v),\quad w=(f,g).
    39	  \]
    40	  The free group preserves $\omega$. For bounded real smooth $b$, the force
    41	  $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$ obeys $\omega(B(b)z,w)+\omega(z,B(b)w) = 0$.
    42	
    43	  Let $1/2 < \theta < 1$ and let $X \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{K}(E))$ start at
    44	  zero, with $U_X$ its left Young evolution. Then
    45	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}
    46	    U_X(t,s)-I\in\mathcal{K}(E),\qquad
    47	    \|S_E(t)U_X(t,s)S_E(-s)\|
    48	    \ge\|S_E(t-s)\|\ge1,\qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
    49	  \end{equation}
    50	  More generally, for finitely many such paths $X_j$ starting at zero on $[0,B]$
    51	  and lengths $0 \le \ell_j \le B$, put $P_j = S_E(\ell_j)U_{X_j}(\ell_j,0)$.
    52	  Then
    53	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}
    54	    P_N\cdots P_0-S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\in\mathcal{K}(E),
    55	    \qquad
    56	    \|P_N\cdots P_0\|
    57	    \ge\left\|S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\right\|\ge1 .
    58	  \end{equation}
    59	  These norm bounds require neither Gaussian nor Hamiltonian operator paths.
    60	\end{lemma}
    61	
    62	\begin{proof}
    63	  The balanced map $C_{\rm bal}(u,v) = (\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v)$ is an
    64	  onto real isometry to $L^2\times L^2$. Define $J_{\rm symp}(q,p) = (p,-q)$ and
    65	  $J_E = C_{\rm bal}^{-1}J_{\rm symp}C_{\rm bal}$. This gives all stated
    66	  operator properties and $J_E(f,g) = (\Lambda^{-1}g,-\Lambda f)$. The two
    67	  displayed dualities follow from the balanced $L^2$ pairing. No $L^2$ pairing
    68	  of a general distributional velocity is taken.
    69	
    70	  In balanced Fourier coordinates, the free matrix is
    71	  \[
    72	    W_t(\xi)=
    73	    \begin{pmatrix}
    74	      \cos(tk)&\langle\xi\rangle\sin(tk)/k\\
    75	      -k\sin(tk)/\langle\xi\rangle&\cos(tk)
    76	    \end{pmatrix},\qquad k=|\xi|.
    77	  \]
    78	  At zero it is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, by
    79	  the continuous sine quotient. Direct matrix multiplication gives
    80	  $W_t^{\mathsf{T}}J_{\rm symp}W_t = J_{\rm symp}$, since its determinant is
    81	  $\cos^2(tk)+\sin^2(tk) = 1$, also at zero. The entries are real, even and
    82	  bounded on finite time horizons. Integrating the identity against real-phase
    83	  Fourier vectors with Hermitian symmetry is legitimate by $L^2$
    84	  Cauchy--Schwarz. It gives $\omega(S_E(t)z,S_E(t)w) = \omega(z,w)$ on all $E$.
    85	  Equivalently one may first use Schwartz phases and then density. No rough
    86	  generator derivative or frequency-zero trace is used.
    87	
    88	  Finally, $\|bu\|_{H^{-1/2}} \le \|bu\|_2 \le \|b\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^{1/2}}$.
    89	  Duality for these $L^2$ functions gives the absolutely integrable cancellation
    90	  $-\int fbu+\int ubf = 0$. This is skewness for $\omega$, not for the $E$
    91	  Hilbert inner product. The Young construction of
    92	  Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear} applies on $\mathcal{L}(E)$: its
    93	  proof uses completeness and operator multiplication of norm one, exactly as on
    94	  $\mathcal{L}(F)$. For fixed $s,t$, each left Young sum
    95	  \[
    96	    \sum_j\big(X(t_{j+1})-X(t_j)\big)U_X(t_j,s)
    97	  \]
    98	  is compact. The sums converge in operator norm to $U_X(t,s)-I$, so closedness
    99	  of the compact ideal gives the first assertion
   100	  in~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}. Bounded composition then shows
   101	  that the physical endpoint differs from $S_E(t-s)$ by a compact operator.
   102	
   103	  We prove the required compact-perturbation bound for this whole-space phase.
   104	  Translations $\tau_y$ on both entries are isometries on $E$ and commute with
   105	  $S_E(h)$. For fixed $z,w \in E$, their translated pairing is the Fourier
   106	  transform of an $L^1$ function: the two weighted Fourier products are
   107	  integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz in the Bessel norms. Approximation of that
   108	  function in $L^1$ by compact smooth functions, followed by integration by

  6278	
  6279	Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  6280	at `a284420`; statement lines 3703-3727 with the display
  6281	`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3718-3724; proof lines 3729-3748), with every
  6282	conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
  6283	3600-3645), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
  6284	facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3730-3731): absolute `L^2` convergence of
  6285	every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
  6286	states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
  6287	`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
  6288	complex `r`, lines 3643-3644) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
  6289	formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
  6290	and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3638-3641). Nothing else about the Gaussian
  6291	field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
  6292	statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
  6293	two facts. For the chain integrals `Y_n` of a centered Gaussian field with
  6294	nonnegative covariance, `TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (wave L8)
  6295	proves `TerminalWickInput` from that lemma's own inputs, and
  6296	`L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` composes the two; the
  6297	identification of the regularized family `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with such terms is
  6298	not formalized. The
  6299	fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
  6300	`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
  6301	`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
  6302	integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
  6303	product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
  6304	`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
  6305	`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
  6306	real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
  6307	`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
  6308	`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
  6309	`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
  6310	the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
  6311	such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
  6312	convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
  6313	in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
  6314	`E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
  6315	absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
  6316	convergence", lines 3735-3736). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
  6317	last sentence (lines 3725-3726): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
  6318	`eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
  6319	(`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
  6320	used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
  6321	`uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
  6322	space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
  6323	hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
  6324	bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
  6325	dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
  6326	are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
  6327	`u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
  6328	(`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
  6329	`B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
  6330	(lines 3738-3745), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
  6331	the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by
  6332	hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every
  6333	`tsum` is a genuine sum; `B >= 0` follows from the moment bound, so

    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}

   116	  -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is

   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,

   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).

   122	  The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   123	  1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   126	  $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   127	
   128	  Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   129	  Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   130	  \[
   131	    \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   132	    \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   133	    \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   134	  \]
   135	  Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
   136	  half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   137	  equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   138	  both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
   139	
   140	  The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
   141	  reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   142	  vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
   143	  because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
   144	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
   145	  q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
   146	  real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The
   147	  following negative upper bound justifies writing that value as
   148	  $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2$ in~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}.
   149	
   150	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial} supplies, for this original
   151	  $\Psi$, one unit compactly supported $w$ and a finite plateau mask with a
   152	  common strictly negative upper bound $\epsilon_0 > 0$. Its trial has support
   153	  in $B_{2L}$; choose its plateau radius $R_0 \ge 2L$. The unmasked form on this
   154	  same $w$ is no larger. Consequently, $-M \le E_s \le -\epsilon_0 < 0$, and
   155	  $\sqrt{\epsilon_0} \le \lambda_{\Psi,s} \le \sqrt M$. Comparing identical unit
   156	  form tests gives $|E_s-E_t| \le \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty$ and therefore
   157	  \[
   158	    |\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{\Psi,t}|
   159	    \le \frac{C_\Psi}{2\sqrt{\epsilon_0}}|s-t|.
   160	  \]

   162	  spectral theorem was applied to $H_s$. This proves
   163	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate}.
   164	\end{proof}

   332	  \label{T:intrinsic-second-moment}
   333	  For every original admissible model with data $(1,0)$ and fixed $x$,
   334	  \begin{equation}\label{E:intrinsic-second-moment-limit}
   335	    \lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-(4-\alpha-a)/(3-\alpha)}
   336	    \log\E|u_\Gamma(T,x)|^2
   337	    =C_2(\Gamma,a)=S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}
   338	    =2^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}.
   339	  \end{equation}
   340	  Its complete variational formula over nonnegative controls is
   341	  \begin{align}
   342	    C_2(\Gamma,a)
   343	    &=\sup_{\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}}
   344	    \left\{2\int_I
   345	    \sqrt{\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   346	    \left(\int h_{\Psi,s}f^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right)}
   347	    \ud s-\frac{v_\Psi}{2}\right\},
   348	    \label{E:intrinsic-positive-formula}\\
   349	    h_{\Psi,s}(x)
   350	    &=\int_I|s-t|^{-a}(\Gamma*\Psi_t)(x)\ud t,\qquad
   351	    v_\Psi=\int_{I\times\R^d}\Psi(s,x)h_{\Psi,s}(x)\ud x\ud s.
